title: Tutorial: Compose Strings With Functions
scenario: Terraform's built-in functions transform values without hardcoding the result. Build a URL-friendly slug from an input, then format a versioned label from that slug.
constraints: Use var.app_name as the source value.
Build local.slug with lower() and replace().

focus.title: Build the derived strings
focus.todo: Create a lowercase, hyphenated slug and a formatted version label.

hints.why: Functions make derived values declarative. A slug built from the same input every time is easier to trust than a value someone copied into the file.
hints.what: Compute two locals. The first should turn the input name into a lowercase string with spaces replaced by hyphens. The second should combine that slug with a version suffix using format().
hints.when: Use string functions when a value is composed from inputs and should update automatically. Avoid them when a plain literal is clearer.
hints.how: Build `slug` first: nest the case-changing function outside the character-replacement function, and pass `var.app_name` as the innermost input. Build `label` with `format()`: the template comes first, followed by `local.slug` and the version suffix. Keep both local names exactly as the outputs expect.
